sources.citation: Reid, Lawrence A. 1994. Possible non-Austronesian lexical elements in Philippine Negrito languages. Oceanic Linguistics 33(1): 37-72 (ScholarSpace author version, hdl 10125/32986, 46 pp. own pagination).
sources.note: Only an editorial convention (author-version p. 10): 'Where stress has been indicated, it is marked as an acute accent on the stressed vowel.' Sec. 2.2.7 'Ayta' (p. 7) notes Wimbish 1986's six Zambales Ayta languages incl. Ambala; Appendix A (p. 30) lists two SIL Ambala wordlists (SBL5 Maliwacat/Cabalan, Olongapo; SBL6 Batong Kalyo (Pili), San Marcelino). No Ambala forms are cited in the data and nothing is said about Ambala stress.

sources.citation: Liwanag, Lolita, Orlando Liwanag, Ranny Liwanag, Terry Liwanag, Zeny Liwanag, Annabel A. Paule & Teresita Rivera. 2017. Manyulat kitamu: Ha' kaparaanan manyulat ya Ayta Ambala [Ayta Ambala Spelling Guide]. 1st ed. City of San Fernando, Pampanga: Department of Education Region III & SIL Philippines. 42 pp. (consultants X. Skoropinski, C. Magaspag, M. Casquite, R. J. F. Gonzales, M. E. Ramos, L. C. Cruz, R. Stone). SIL Language & Culture Archives 74615.
sources.note: Orthography guide only: 4 vowels (a, i, u, ê [as Ilocano e]), 15 consonants incl. glottal stop written with an apostrophe medially after a consonant and word-finally (bung'uy, kadê'); rules on Ciy spelling, enclitic pronoun -ku/-yaku/-waku/-aku, markers hay/ya', linker ya' > a'/y, loan letters e/o, punctuation; sample sentences and texts. No accent marks are used and nothing is said about stress (no 'diin'/'tuldik' section).

sources.citation: Himes, Ronald S. 2012. The Central Luzon group of languages. Oceanic Linguistics 51(2): 490-537.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: a digital copy exists, behind a library sign-in (also a publisher record (DOI), probably paywalled)
sources.note: The only modern comparative treatment with first-hand Ambala data (Pastolan, Gordon Heights); Himes's OL papers give per-language sound correspondences and typically remark on accent/stress reflexes, so it is the likeliest place a statement on Ambala stress exists.

sources.citation: Greenhill, Simon J., Robert Blust & Russell D. Gray. 2008-. Austronesian Basic Vocabulary Database (ABVD); CLDF release lexibank/abvd. Lists 1263 'Ayta Ambala' (source Stone 2008, SPLC 19), 1270 'Alangan' (source Barbian 1977), 418 'Gaddang' (Troyer in Reid 1971).

sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 2.2 'Ayta Ambala' (p. 2) gives only speakers/location (citing Ramos 2004); the paper is a lexical comparison by grammatical category, zero hits for stress/accent/penult/suprasegmental. Earlier an earlier compilation read the 2008 SPLC version and found the same.

sources.citation: SIL Philippines. 1988. Ayta Ambala survey wordlist, Bayan Bayanan, Dinalupihan, Bataan (form dated 4-7-88; English-Tagalog-Cebuano elicitation sheet with handwritten Ambala column), 19 pp. Collection of Unpublished Materials, SIL International - Philippines (= SIL Language & Culture Archives 'Ayta, Ambala - Bayan Bayanan wordlist', entry 79916).
sources.note: Wordlist-only: handwritten Ambala forms carry acute stress marks on both penultimate and final syllables (p. 2: anlú 'day/sun', yábi 'night', lángit 'sky', úlap 'cloud', kílat/kimát 'lightning', lindól 'earthquake', báto 'stone', buhángin 'sand', pútik 'mud'); no phonological notes or statement. Scan has no usable text for the Ambala column (handwriting).

sources.citation: Wimbish, John S. 1986. The languages of the Zambales mountains: A Philippine lexicostatistic study. Work Papers of the SIL, UND Session 30: 133-142.
sources.note: First delineation of Ambala as a language, based on SIL wordlists; may note transcription conventions (stress marks). Open PDF exists but the host's bot challenge blocked download.

sources.citation: Reed, William Allan. 1904. Negritos of Zambales. (Department of the Interior, Ethnological Survey Publications, vol. II, part I.) Manila: Bureau of Public Printing. Appendix B 'Vocabularies' (Zambal of Bolinao, Zambal of Iba, Zambal-Aeta, Aeta of Santa Fe, Aeta of Subig, Aeta of Bataan, Dumagat of Bulacan). Project Gutenberg EBook #20329.
sources.note: marks only: every form is syllabified with an accent mark (la-la'-ki, ha-bot', ba-bay'-e..), no statement about accent; prose says the Zambales Negritos 'seem to have lost entirely their own language and to have adopted that of the Christianized Zambal' and that the Santa Fe and Subig vocabularies 'do not differ materially from the Zambal-Aeta'.

sources.citation: Kern, H. 1882. Over de taal der Philippijnsche Negrito's. Bijdragen tot de Taal-, Land- en Volkenkunde 30: 243-261.
sources.note: Earliest linguistic discussion of Zambales/Bataan Negrito material (Meyer's lists); Kern sometimes comments on 'klemtoon'. Open access at Brill in principle but the site refuses automated downloads.
